sections.title: A world made one tile at a time
paragraphs: Atmospheric medieval fantasy at a practical native scale. Forest paths lead to warm workshops, weathered settlements and dangerous ruins. Characters carry identity through silhouette and equipment; terrain supports the action without demanding attention from every pixel. The influence of Baldur’s Gate 3 concerns worldbuilding, architecture and environmental storytelling, translated into an original traditional top-down RPG.

sections.title: The visual hierarchy
paragraphs: Apply this order during every review: visual consistency, gameplay readability, reusable construction, character identity, environmental atmosphere, then decorative detail. A beautiful sprite with a shifted ground anchor fails before color polish is considered. A road with visible seams fails before flowers are added.

Aim for a substantial fantasy RPG built from a manageable library. Use broad grass masses, clustered tree canopies, timber and stone structures, deliberate warm windows and restrained landmarks. Ordinary ground stays quieter than bodies, hands, tools and danger indicators.

sections.title: Top-down camera contract
paragraphs: Use an orthogonal, traditional top-down presentation with visible front faces on characters and buildings. Keep verticals vertical. Ground cells remain squares in map space. Roofs show a simple top plane; walls show enough front face to communicate entry height. This is an artistic oblique view without isometric diamond coordinates or cinematic convergence.

The study buildings use a 5×5-tile visual envelope including roof and front face. Their traversable footprint is a separate plan. Apply the same slope convention within a building kit; never rescale a roof to fit a wall. Cardinal doors must meet ground paths on tile boundaries. Diagonal movement does not rotate the camera or terrain.

sections.title: Storytelling at moderate detail
paragraphs: Tell a workshop story with a broad apron silhouette, an anvil, stacked timber and one warm working light. Use a repaired beam and clean road edge to signal restoration. Avoid lore written in tiny decoration: an artist may suggest age through broken geometry and muted moss without inventing historical events or named factions.

At 1×, a player should distinguish the route, doorway, resource and enemy before noticing surface grain. Reserve the strongest local contrast for actors and interactables. Each decorative cluster should reinforce mass, material, light or use.

sections.title: Rejected treatments
paragraphs: The comparison moves from grouped foliage to noisy foliage, inconsistent internal pixel size and excessive gradients. Reject each failure on its own: noise competes with action; doubled pixels break density; gradients introduce too many values for a small form. The rejected cells are teaching examples, never production targets.

pages.title: Pixel scale, bounds and anchors
pages.summary: A sprite cell is a container. Its visible body, contact point and collision are different measurements.

sections.title: Native pixels and display pixels
paragraphs: One native pixel is one sample in the source PNG. At integer display scale 4, that sample occupies a 4×4 block of screen pixels. A 16×16 tile becomes 64×64 screen pixels, and a 32-pixel-tall body becomes 128 screen pixels tall. This does not change either source asset. A 1.5× scale gives alternating sample widths and is unsuitable as a production correction.

Keep sprite and terrain transforms at the agreed native relationship. A tree drawn with 2×2 chunks masquerading as single pixels does not become compatible by shrinking its node. Redraw the tree with the same one-pixel units as the character.

sections.title: A measured coordinate contract
paragraphs: Recommended character frame coordinates use a top-left origin (0,0), x right and y down. Reserve a 64×64 transparent cell; place standing contact at (32,48). The original study has its head near y17 and feet near y47, so visible height is about 31 pixels while the cell remains 64 pixels tall. Action reach may occupy the margin, but the body must not drift to recenter a sword.

Bounds are half-open rectangles [x,y,width,height]. An occupied pixel at x37 belongs to a bound ending at x38. The visual union includes hair and equipment; the collision reference covers only the walkable body footprint. Ground contact stays stable through a walk; a jump or dodge may lift the body while its ground shadow and root remain registered.

sections.title: World scale ladder
paragraphs: A humanoid is roughly two terrain tiles tall. A 16-pixel icon is a symbolic inventory view and does not measure the world sword. A small crate is typically 16×16 or 32×32; furniture seats should accept the same body. Doors start at 16 pixels clear width and 32 pixels visible height when using a taller modular door kit. The small atlas doorway is a construction study requiring an extended door for final character clearance.

Use 16-pixel multiples for large prop canvases and building modules. Tree canopies vary by species; the 48×64 study is a recommended size, not a measured game tree. A boss may exceed a 64-pixel canvas while keeping one-pixel edges and the same material cluster scale.

sections.title: Camera and resolution decisions
paragraphs: Candidate 320×180 shows a compact 20×11.25-tile field; 384×216 shows 24×13.5; 480×270 shows 30×16.875. Fractional tile counts at viewport edges are normal. Compare action reach, readable text, UI occupancy and 30-actor crowd tests before selecting a logical resolution. These are tuning examples, not final settings.

A 1920×1080 output can display 320×180 at 6×, 384×216 at 5× or 480×270 at 4×. On other screens, use a documented integer viewport scale with letterboxing or a reviewed expanded field. Camera zoom multiplies display scale; 2× camera zoom at 4× viewport scaling yields 8 screen pixels per native pixel. Godot stretch mode and camera policy still need runtime verification.

sections.title: Artist measurement procedure
steps: Open the export with a visible one-pixel grid. Count the visible body height, then measure canvas separately.
Overlay a 16×16 grid and the (32,48) contact cross. Compare all frames and all equipment on that cross.
Place character, door, tree, weapon and ground together at 1×. Compare pixels inside each object, not just total size.
Preview integer display scales without resizing sources. Reject filtered, nonuniform or subpixel placement artifacts.

pages.summary: Build readable masses before texture, and use each pixel to clarify shape or material.

sections.title: Cluster construction
paragraphs: Draw the silhouette as a single mass, divide it into lit and shadow planes, then add only clusters that describe curvature or a material break. A useful leaf cluster is a connected 3–8-pixel shape with a stepped edge, not a scatter of single bright dots. At 1×, each cluster should join a larger canopy mass.

Remove isolated pixels unless they explain an eye, fastening, spark or one-pixel edge correction. Avoid repeated diagonal stair steps that form unintended stripes. Check negative space between legs, under arms and around tools. One pixel can open a pose; ten extra highlights can close it.

sections.title: Enlarged cluster practice
paragraphs: Use the viewer’s 8× zoom and pixel grid to inspect connected shapes; use 1× to decide whether they work. The grass tile places short connected blades within broad quiet color. The tree repeats broad lobes with irregular silhouette breaks. Neither requires a different shade on every leaf.

A good practice pass removes half the interior texture and keeps the form intact. If removing texture destroys recognition, improve the silhouette. If repeated terrain forms a checker pattern, lower interior contrast or offer compatible alternatives rather than hiding the tile boundary with more noise.

sections.title: Selective one-pixel outlines
paragraphs: Start small characters with selective one-pixel colored outlines. Use deep blue, green or brown shadows related to the material; keep true black exceptional. Darken the lower-right edge and gear overlap, and open or lighten the upper-left edge where the form meets bright light.

Interior outlines separate an arm from a tunic or a blade from a torso. They should disappear where surfaces share the same plane. Against bright snow, preserve a dark-side contour. Against dark forest ground, retain a light-facing shoulder or hair edge. Do not solve every background by enclosing every object in solid black.

sections.title: Four purposeful values
paragraphs: Use three to five meaningful shades per ordinary material as an initial guideline. In the study ramps, shadow separates, shade turns the plane, body carries local color and light names the lit plane. Shift hue with value: cool blue-green shadows beneath warmer yellow-green leaves, cooler metal shade beneath a pale reflection.

Assume a soft upper-left daylight direction for baked form shading. Runtime lights add broad local mood without moving every painted highlight. Metal uses a small hard light edge; bark uses broken vertical planes; cloth uses larger folds; stone uses irregular flat facets. A metal highlight that covers half the blade reads as white plastic.

sections.title: Repair a failed sprite
steps: Flatten the image to a single silhouette and identify ambiguous appendages. Redraw the large shape first.
Reduce material colors into coherent ramps; eliminate near-duplicate values that add no plane change.
Align light-facing planes to upper-left. Keep contact shadows tight beneath objects.
Remove random dithering, double outlines and alternating single-pixel texture. Recheck 1× contrast against grass, stone and snow.
Export at native size and compare without browser smoothing. A blurred preview cannot establish a crisp source.

pages.title: Palette, ramps and recoloring
pages.summary: A cohesive proposed palette with explicit uses, downloadable swatches and owner approval boundaries.
pages.maturity: Edition 0.1.0 · Owner review pending for new reference art

sections.title: Briarwake Study 01
paragraphs: This 56-color palette is a proposed reference created for these examples. It is not an owner-approved master palette. Four entries per material provide a common shadow-to-light structure. Materials may share colors in future revisions; a 56-entry library does not mean using all colors on one sprite.

Keep quiet ground within a narrow value band. Lift actors through silhouette and local contrast rather than saturation alone. Danger uses shape, motion and a clear edge alongside color; never depend solely on red-versus-green. Magical colors should not become ordinary ground noise.

sections.title: Material ramps
paragraphs: Read each ramp from shadow to light. Grass is lower-frequency ground; leaves carry stronger grouped shapes above it. Earth and leather differ in contrast and surface treatment even when their hue families overlap. Metal and water share cool relationships but have different reflection geometry. Fire and magic have restricted bright activation pixels.

sections.title: Load and preserve the palette in Aseprite
steps: Download the local GPL palette. In the palette options, load it; verify the first and last color against this specification. Save a named project palette copy.
Use RGB mode for layered authoring unless an indexed workflow is required. RGB permits deliberate color sampling; check the export’s distinct opaque colors afterward.
In indexed mode, reserve a transparent index and review palette remapping before changing entries. A palette reorder can alter an indexed image if indices are remapped incorrectly.
Use contiguous ramp selections for controlled recolor variants. Preserve light order and material distinctions. Review colors against representative ground.
Do not paste third-party art into the study palette or use color reduction as a substitute for rights clearance. Record any added color as a proposed palette revision.

sections.title: Regional and lighting variation
paragraphs: Forests emphasize leaves, wood and earth; mountains emphasize stone with cooler shadows; marshes use lower-value grass and subdued water; coastlines use pale earth and cool water; settlements warm wood and brick; ruins mute stone beneath leaf accents. These are ramp relationships, not new canonical places.

Lighting examples reuse one map and alter its presentation. Dusk and rain reduce contrast, night preserves actor edges, snow shifts broad ground values and torchlight introduces a bounded warm area. Derived lighting colors are preview outputs and are exempt from the master-source palette check; do not sample them back into ordinary source sprites.

sections.title: Palette acceptance
paragraphs: Before adopting a new master palette, compare terrain repetition, all skin ramps, cloth/armor differentiation, night readability and danger indicators. Submit a named revision with affected assets, a remap table and rollback plan. Owner approval must name the exact palette version. A documentation commit alone cannot grant that approval.

pages.summary: Reusable 16×16 cells, complete terrain families and exact scene recipes.

sections.title: Start with the atlas
paragraphs: The example atlas is 256×256 pixels: 16 columns by 16 rows of 16×16 cells, zero margin and zero spacing. Atlas coordinates are zero-based. Native pixel origin is top-left. The region at cell (c,r) is [16c,16r,16,16]. Empty cells remain fully transparent and are not production tiles.

Rows 0–9, columns 0–2 hold three variants of grass, dirt, packed earth, mud, stone, cobblestone, sand, snow, forest ground and marsh ground. Four water frames occupy (4,0) through (7,0). Building modules start at (4,2). The gallery exposes the exact cell dictionary; avoid guessing from a scaled preview.

sections.title: Ten complete study families
paragraphs: Every family includes a base, two quiet variations and all 47 gated neighbor masks in the companion transition atlas. Decoration overlays are separate reusable natural objects. Marsh ground shares the grass family’s dark relationship; snow uses the pale metal ramp as a technical color study, pending palette review.

sections.title: Repeat before decorating
paragraphs: Inspect one tile at 1×, a 3×3 repeat and a 10×10 repeat. Large shapes near the edge must connect intentionally; avoid bright features centered identically in every tile. The identical-repeat image exposes periodic texture honestly. In a mixed area, use two or three variants with a quiet base weighted most often. Do not randomize every pixel.

The study uses deterministic placement so every screenshot is reproducible. A production terrain set may use alternative tile probabilities for compatible variants, after testing the selected Godot version. Changes to boundary shape require corresponding terrain patterns, not a random alternative.

sections.title: Proof of modularity
paragraphs: Both village compositions use the same atlas, transitions and object library. Roofs, wall faces, stairs, signs and bridges are placed as named cells. Trees and bushes are independent reusable PNGs. Each map records every tile and object position. No image is a painted background. The scenes demonstrate construction and scale; owner art approval remains pending.

sections.title: Atlas delivery contract
steps: Deliver the editable atlas source and the native PNG with the same cell geometry. Include a cell-name dictionary and a list of deliberately empty cells.
Keep whole cells; no packing, rotation, trimming or automatic cell deduplication unless coordinate metadata is revised and reviewed.
Place animated sequences in the documented order. The study water strip is four 16×16 frames at 160 ms each; visual loop review remains required.
Submit a seam test, mixed-terrain map, crossing, isolated patch and shoreline. Mark collisions, navigation and occlusion as separate integration notes.
Record grid size, texture margin, separation, source hash and revision. A PNG without its source association fails handoff.

pages.title: Transitions, corners and path networks
pages.summary: All 47 neighbor patterns, exact coordinates and a repeatable method for boundary tests.
pages.maturity: Edition 0.1.0 · Owner review pending for new reference art

sections.title: The complete pattern convention
paragraphs: Use an eight-neighbor blob convention with bits N=1, NE=2, E=4, SE=8, S=16, SW=32, W=64, NW=128. The center belongs to the foreground terrain. A diagonal bit is retained only when both adjacent cardinal bits are present. For example, keep NE only if N and E are present. Enumerating masks 0–255 and gating corners leaves exactly 47 unique patterns.

Mask 0 is an isolated patch; 255 is fully surrounded; masks with one cardinal connection form dead ends; opposing connections form narrow corridors; three and four connections support junctions. Missing diagonal bits between present sides produce concave corners. Outer corners are convex boundaries. Repeated stair-step placement of corner patterns provides pixel diagonals without rotating tiles. This is a two-material overlay convention, not a complete three-material Godot terrain solver.

sections.title: Atlas lookup and corner ownership
paragraphs: The transition PNG is 256×480: ten family blocks of three rows each. Within a family, sort the 47 masks numerically. For index i, column is i mod 16 and row is 3×familyIndex + floor(i/16). Slot 47 in each 48-cell block is empty. The local metadata records mask-to-cell coordinates for all 470 filled slots.

Each transition is an alpha overlay over another base family, so dirt can blend into grass or forest ground can meet water. Use a consistent foreground priority per terrain pair. A cell’s center and all neighbor bits must be documented together. At a three-way junction, choose a base layer, add one terrain overlay, then a second with a reviewed overlap rule; do not claim all multi-terrain cases are covered by a binary set.

sections.title: Boundaries, crossings and shorelines
paragraphs: A path crossing requires continuous cardinal connectors and concave corner variants around the remaining ground islands. An isolated patch needs no side connectors. A one-cell-wide path uses opposing side bits with no unsupported diagonal. Test both a one-cell and two-cell neck: a rounded border must not consume the whole route. Shorelines use the same mask logic with water beneath, plus separate reed or foam accents.

For diagonal boundaries, alternate stair steps with matching corner patterns. Do not use 45-degree rotated 16×16 tiles: that changes the grid, creates resampling and breaks neighbors. At intersections of unlike roads, decide which material owns the center before painting the map.

sections.title: Godot terrain peering is a separate mapping
paragraphs: Godot 4.7 TileSet terrain modes describe corners and sides. The binary neighbor mask in this guide is an authoring convention; a programmer or technical artist must assign the correct terrain center and peering bits in TileData. Do not paste the integer mask into an arbitrary terrain field and expect automatic behavior.

Use Match Corners and Sides only after mapping the complete chosen set and empty terrain meaning. Test paint, erase, narrow routes, inside corners, map borders and all orientations. If a terrain solver requests unsupported multi-material combinations, expand the kit or constrain the tool deliberately. Keep a manual stamped test map as a reference alongside the terrain painting test.

sections.title: Transition acceptance checklist
bullets: Exactly 47 unique gated masks per family; no duplicate mask IDs or silently empty required patterns.
Opposite edges of repeating base tiles match. Crossings and isolated patches preserve their intended width.
Transparent edges reveal the correct lower layer, without dark matte pixels or gaps.
Outer and inner corners read at 1×; decorative overlays do not hide missing geometry.
Terrain painting in Godot must be tested separately; the shipped PNG and static checks do not certify peering integration.

sections.title: Water family construction
paragraphs: Use broad horizontal masses for water. A pond or lake combines a quiet base, a shallow shelf, a deep-water interior and a complete shoreline overlay. Rivers reuse these pieces with directional accent strips. Coastlines use a wider shallow band and optional low-frequency foam. Marsh water lowers contrast and shares reed and mud relationships.

The study atlas contains a four-frame horizontal water accent loop. Use 160 ms per frame as a tuning example; the reflection must return without a jump. Shallow and deep-water palettes, flow arrows and waterfall motion are production specifications requiring further authored variants; the still water demonstration is not a complete running-water or waterfall kit.

sections.title: Elevation without perspective drift
paragraphs: A cliff face consumes screen height while its top footprint stays on the 16×16 map grid. Use repeatable vertical bands, corner caps and a distinct top rim. Start with a 16-pixel face height as a recommended kit unit; stack bands for taller cliffs rather than scaling one face. A stair strip must meet both lower and upper ground boundaries.

Show where a character stands at the top and base. The artist supplies visible rim, contact and obstruction suggestions; gameplay decides traversability and actual collision. Avoid painting a dark stripe that reads as an impassable wall if it is meant to be walkable terrain.

sections.title: Edges affect gameplay integration
paragraphs: Deliver a marked preview for collision, navigation, occlusion and interaction separately. A waterfall can be a visual sprite behind a traversable bridge; a shoreline may allow fishing without walking. A canopy or cliff overhang may hide a player and needs a foreground or fade treatment. None of those behaviors are guaranteed by the PNG.

Bank connection pixels and bridge origins must remain compatible across damaged and restored states. Any changed navigation area must be identified in the handoff, not embedded as an unexplained color change.

steps: Place a 10×10 base water repeat with a full shoreline on each side, including concave bays and isolated islands.
Play water tiles beside the shore: the shore remains registered and reflection accents do not creep across boundaries.
Test the flow strip, crest, waterfall body and splash as separate modules. Match loop duration or document independent periods.
Place a 32-pixel character at banks, stairs, bridge rails and cave mouths. Check visibility at 1× and request engine traversal review.

sections.title: Tree construction standard
paragraphs: The proposed deciduous study uses a 48×64 canvas with clustered canopy lobes, a 5–8-pixel main trunk and contact near (24,60). The canopy is a visual mass, not the collision shape. Reserve a suggested 2×1-tile root footprint; final collision is reviewed by gameplay. An evergreen uses stacked tapered clusters at the same native density. Dead trees use branch silhouette rather than a leaf texture recolor.

Paint upper-left highlights in broad connected patches, darker leaf separation at the lower-right and a small ground shadow. Avoid a bright highlight on every leaf. Vary silhouette and canopy lobe placement between trees while retaining trunk scale. A large ancient tree needs a larger canvas and authored structure, not a rescaled small tree.

sections.title: Ground contact and sorting
paragraphs: Deliver the trunk and canopy together for a simple static object, with a ground anchor at the root contact. For roofs or canopies that must reveal characters, split foreground canopy from the trunk while keeping identical coordinates and an explicit registration reference. Keep contact shadows distinct from overhead foliage.

Y-sort at root contact rather than top-left or image bottom by accident. A character behind the trunk should pass behind it; a character below it should draw in front unless a deliberate overhead canopy covers them. Shared z_index and parent y_sort_enabled conditions require engine verification. Collision should usually cover the trunk base, not the canopy silhouette.

sections.title: Sparse, normal and dense placement
paragraphs: Sparse placement leaves broad grass between one tree, a few stones and an herb patch. Normal placement groups trees in twos or threes around a clear route, with intermittent low props. Dense placement overlaps canopies at the map edge but preserves a visible travel corridor and combat clearance. Density refers to objects per area, not extra texture per tile.

Build forest, marsh and mountain edges from the same library by changing the ratio and palette relationships: deciduous clusters in forest, dead trunks and reeds in marsh, evergreen and rock in mountains. Recolor variants require palette review and should not erase species silhouette.

sections.title: Resource state contract
paragraphs: A gatherable object needs a readable available and depleted state where gameplay requires it. For ore, remove the bright ore cluster without shifting the rock contact; for berries, keep the bush silhouette and remove fruit; for trees, align the stump with the trunk root. Do not require every decorative object to own resource state.

Submit the state names, root position and any intended obstacle change. A depleted tree becoming a stump may change collision, but the authoritative resource or world system decides when that occurs. Avoid decorative flowers that use the same highlight as an active gathering marker.

sections.title: A complete building kit
paragraphs: Start with a common 16×16 module and native density. A kit needs walls, inside and outside corners, foundations, doors, windows, roof centers, roof edges, ridge and eave pieces. Chimneys, shutters, support beams, pillars, stairs, fences and signs are independent additions. Some demonstration pieces share geometry; that does not remove their semantic role from the cell dictionary.

The study house uses a 5×5-tile visual envelope: a three-row roof, one front wall row and a foundation/stair row. It is a compact construction proof. Production door and wall variants must be extended to the character-clearance standard before runtime approval. Keep roof and body widths compatible instead of stretching an assembled PNG.

sections.title: Assembly recipe
steps: Reserve an 80×80 visual envelope on a 5×5 grid. Choose an entrance at column 2 of the front face.
Stamp five ridge cells on roof row 0. On row 1 use left edge, three roof centers and right edge. Stamp eave cells on row 2.
Stamp wall corners at columns 0 and 4 of row 3, windows at 1 and 3 and the doorway at 2. On row 4 use foundations and the centered stair.
Add the chimney above the wall plane and a sign beside the entrance. Record any sorting overlap.
Repeat the same pieces for a second placement; vary frontage accessories and layout before commissioning an entirely new atlas.

sections.title: Footprints and connection points
paragraphs: Record visual bounds, grid footprint, entrance cells and floor threshold separately. A 5×5 exterior envelope is not a 5×5 collision rectangle. Roof overhang and front wall height change the image without changing walkable interior area. Doors connect to paths at whole-cell boundaries. Fences require ends, corners and gate-compatible connections.

Prepare alternate roof visibility when buildings can contain players. Split a roof into its own aligned layer or sprite, and record which contact line governs sorting. Technical artists test player occlusion and doorway passage. Never bake interface interaction markers permanently into a building sprite.

sections.title: Settlement composition
paragraphs: Group structures around readable circulation. Leave at least a two-cell visual route for ordinary travel as a recommended starting point, then test actual player and collision widths. Keep stalls and foliage from blocking sight to doors. Use signs and one warm window to establish purpose. Repeated buildings should vary frontage and placement rather than pixel density.

Review both settlement scenes side by side. The second uses the same roof, wall, bridge and prop assets in a new arrangement. A new settlement should first exhaust layout and material variations before adding a large new kit.

sections.title: Interior grid and floor plans
paragraphs: Keep the 16×16 grid indoors. Do not enlarge characters or furniture to fill a room. A recommended small workshop plan is 8×6 tiles: one front entrance, a two-cell circulation strip, a two-by-one workbench against the back wall, storage along one side and clear floor for a standing character. A cottage can start at 6×5; an inn common room at 12×8. These are tuning examples rather than canonical buildings.

Use repeatable wood or stone floor tiles with quiet seams. Back walls may occupy two visual tile rows while their ground contact occupies one boundary. Corner and doorway pieces must preserve the same face depth as the exterior kit. Provide a plan and an assembled preview; a painted room PNG alone is insufficient.

sections.title: Character visibility and draw order
paragraphs: Separate the base floor, ground rug, furniture, back walls, front wall and overhead ceiling/roof. Ground rugs stay below feet. Tables and chairs sort by their contact line. Foreground walls and tall shelves may need a cutaway or fade when the player stands behind them. Artists provide compatible alternate art; programmers control visibility.

Do not let a decorative foreground silhouette cover interaction prompts or combat tells. Test a 32-pixel body beside every tall item and between chair and table. Keep collision reference guides out of PNG export.

sections.title: Light and material consistency
paragraphs: Use baked upper-left form shading on furniture even when a warm lamp provides runtime mood. Window light can be a reusable overlay with a sharp or deliberately stepped pixel boundary. Avoid soft gradients painted across the floor atlas: they repeat badly and bind a room to one lighting setup.

Distinguish service objects by silhouette and a small material cue. An alchemy bench may use bottles; a smithing area uses dark metal and a warm heat accent; a cooking area uses wood, stone and cookware. Vocation styling must not invent mandatory gameplay equipment or a new station ownership system.

sections.title: Construction measurements
paragraphs: Use the following as proposed construction measurements for new artwork, not measurements of unavailable purchased sprites. The study body’s head occupies about 11×11 pixels including hair. Neck and shoulders lead into a 10–13-pixel torso width; arms are about 3 pixels wide; legs use two separated 3-pixel columns. Hands and feet are compact 2–4-pixel groups. Overall standing height is approximately 32 pixels.

At this scale, face identity comes from head contour, hair, skin ramp and one- or two-pixel feature placement. Do not add a detailed face that forces an enlarged head or destroys body clearance. Hair volume can extend beyond the body bound, but it must leave room for headwear.

sections.title: Base-body contract
paragraphs: The base body defines contact (32,48), head placement, shoulder and wrist attachment regions and action registration. Document any intentional body movement per frame. Clothes follow that body; they do not recenter the frame. Keep standing feet stable at the contact line, allowing the expected one-pixel walk bob.

A base must be tested nude or in a neutral underlayer across all facing directions before outfits are commissioned. Check separated limbs in silhouette. Skin palette variants should preserve value order. The blank and study Aseprite templates provide a starting coordinate contract, not approved race anatomy.

sections.title: Human, Goblin and Demon evidence
paragraphs: The inspected game commit contains project configuration and editor integration, but no Human, Goblin or Demon sheets, hairstyles, cloaks, outfits or creator guides. Therefore this edition cannot verify race appearance, body dimensions, anatomy differences, sheet size, frame durations or layer compatibility. No horns, ears, limb proportions or skin colors are presented as measured race facts.

When the owner supplies licensed local sources, inventory each race’s native canvas, visible bounds, contact, action/facing coverage, palette, layer order and creator notes. Keep paid sheets private until redistribution and AI-workflow terms are checked. Race redesign is a separate approval decision; retain equipment and animation compatibility unless a reviewed new base contract replaces it.

sections.title: A shared registration space
paragraphs: Start with body, outfit, hair and equipment layers in the same 64×64 coordinates. All visible components share action, facing, frame identity and duration. Select one timeline and update every visual layer from it. Independent AnimatedSprite2D playback per garment can drift and is not an acceptable synchronization contract. The art source determines which frame belongs to which action.

Set each frame duration in milliseconds. Preview at source speed and check the first/last-frame join. Do not add a duplicate first frame that creates an unintended hold.
Create tags such as walk_s and attack_ne with inclusive start and end frames. Export tags and per-frame duration metadata.

sections.title: Existing cardinal art and the eight-direction target
paragraphs: The owner’s requested audit includes four-direction existing art, six-frame walk cycles, running conventions and creator-recommended durations. None can be verified from the inspected repository because those sources are absent. Treat those statements as requested audit targets. Do not convert them into confirmed inventory facts. The new study has six-frame walks by design, not as evidence about legacy assets.

The release target names N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W and NW. Author diagonal head orientation, torso angle, visible shoulder, far-arm overlap, leg stride, feet and equipment alignment. A diagonal is not a cardinal sprite rotated, skewed or shifted sideways. Mirroring may support deliberate symmetric work only after asymmetric gear and light are corrected. Do not label four cardinal rows as eight genuine directions.

sections.title: Source tags and runtime identifiers
paragraphs: Use lower_snake_case tags action_facing, for example walk_s or cast_nw. A source can group several actions; the runtime may use a structured action/facing key. Record the exact mapping instead of assuming the tag name is automatically imported. Aseprite frame duration is milliseconds; Godot playback resources need a reviewed conversion.

A fixed-grid sheet preserves cell coordinates. Individual frames are easier to inspect but increase file count. Packed or trimmed sheets require explicit frame rectangles and original-canvas offsets. Prefer untrimmed grid cells for paper-doll registration. Do not enable Aseprite deduplication if it would remove frame identity expected by the importer.

sections.title: Godot playback options
paragraphs: AnimatedSprite2D with SpriteFrames is suitable for a simple flattened character. SpriteFrames can define animations and per-frame duration multipliers; use an explicit conversion from milliseconds to resource playback timing and check elapsed loop time. AnimationPlayer can coordinate multiple Sprite2D frame, visibility and equipment tracks on one timeline. Neither approach requires a third-party plugin by default.

PNG export does not transfer Aseprite layers, tags or events automatically. If consuming JSON, document the importer and validate rectangles, durations, tags and offsets. In the engine, test action interruption, terminal death poses, facing swaps and synchronized equipment. These tests are not established by the HTML viewer.

Recovery reduces brightness and returns attention to actors. Not every effect needs equal time in every phase: a hit spark may be mostly impact and recovery.

Use hard pixel edges, deliberate clusters and transparent backgrounds. Semi-transparent source pixels are acceptable only when they form intentional stepped fades; never use resampling blur. sections.title: Multiplayer overlap budget
paragraphs: In a 30-player composition, effects should expose actor centers and important ground boundaries. Reserve priority for local danger and immediate impacts; decorative auras can have fewer opaque pixels. An open-ring effect often preserves feet better than a filled disk. Art supplies density variants; gameplay chooses presentation based on its existing systems.

Test two players attacking, a party surrounding an enemy and many players at an objective. Review effect overlap against terrain and foreground props. Do not interpret a static stress scene as a performance test or a guarantee of target capacity.

sections.title: Aseprite source and export
paragraphs: Use a canvas that contains the full effect at native density; 64×64 is an initial work size, not a universal limit. Name tags by effect phase where independent playback is needed. Anchor a swing to the shared weapon/body coordinates; anchor a ground area effect to its ground center. Record frames, durations, loop behavior and intended layer.

Export explicit PNG frames or an untrimmed sheet with JSON. Keep source colors separate from runtime tint. If the effect must be tinted in Godot, document which pixels form the value mask and verify the shader or modulate path in-engine. Do not require a custom plugin for a simple sprite effect.

sections.title: Visual acceptance
paragraphs: An effect fails if it hides critical attacks, uses inconsistent internal pixel sizes, clips at the frame edge, moves off its attachment point or relies solely on color for danger. sections.title: Weather and seasonal modules
paragraphs: Rain uses sparse short pixel streaks and optional small impact accents, separate from terrain. Snow uses authored ground and roof variants plus restrained flakes; a cool color wash is not a complete winter kit. Fog uses bounded low-frequency layers with reviewed opacity and edge treatment. Wind changes foliage or cloth through small authored poses, not elastic image distortion.

Autumn foliage should preserve value order and trunk relationships while changing leaf ramps. Winter needs bare-tree or snow-loaded variants, clear doors and visible road boundaries. Keep transitions complete: a snow base without snow-to-road, snow-to-water and roof-edge states is incomplete. Match seasonal objects to the same contact and footprint contract.

sections.title: Set up the working file
steps: Create a new RGB document with transparent background and exact native dimensions. Save immediately as .aseprite in the source directory.
Set grid width and height to 16, with origin at (0,0). Turn on the grid when checking atlas alignment; toggle it off for silhouette review.
Load the named project palette. Record the palette ID and revision in the asset handoff.
Name visual layers by responsibility. Use body, hair, outfit, cloak_back, headwear, equipment_front, shadow and effects only where needed.
Keep guides and collision_ref hidden and explicitly excluded from exports. Reference layers explain integration but do not define authoritative collision.
Save an incremental revision before changing canvas size, palette, frame order or tags. Preserve the previous approved source until migration is reviewed.

sections.title: Frames, onion skin and tags
paragraphs: Use the timeline to add or duplicate frames. Duplicate registered layers together; avoid copying a garment into a different-size document. Set frame duration explicitly, then use onion skinning to check motion arcs and contact. Tags use action_facing such as walk_s and cast_ne, with inclusive endpoints. Source tags and runtime identifiers are mapped in metadata rather than assumed identical.

Inspect the first and last frames together for loops. For nonlooping death or impact, record terminal hold behavior. Play each direction at 1× before exporting. A six-frame source is not automatically a 6 fps animation: six 100 ms frames make a 600 ms cycle.

sections.title: Tilemap editing and atlas maintenance
paragraphs: In Aseprite 1.3+, create a tilemap layer with a 16×16 tileset when that editing mode helps reuse. Understand whether edits update a shared tile or create a new tile; test on a duplicate source first. Keep intentional alternative tiles separate and preserve stable atlas IDs.

An Aseprite editing tilemap is not a Godot TileSet resource. Export a documented PNG atlas and map its cells in Godot separately. Do not claim terrain peering, collisions, navigation or tile IDs transfer automatically. The supplied atlas studies use normal image layers and are not falsely labeled native tilemap documents.

sections.title: Export without changing pixel identity
steps: Save the editable source. Hide guide layers and select the intended tag or state.
Use sprite-sheet export with a fixed grid layout at 100% scale. Keep trim, packing, rotation, border and shape padding disabled for shared paper-doll cells.
Export PNG with alpha. Export JSON array metadata including frame rectangles, durations and tags when required.
For individual frames, use a zero-padded action/facing/frame naming pattern. Export related layers with identical cells and frame order.
Reopen the PNG and compare native dimensions, transparent margins, colors, loop duration and source contact. Keep a preview separate from runtime exports.

sections.title: Version evidence
paragraphs: The read-only game project at commit 923c52d6959348b42b4fa8744878afd5f3d8c40c declares config/features 4.7 and canvas_items stretch with expand aspect. The installed Godot binary reports 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf. The project does not pin a patch version or final viewport dimensions. This chapter uses the official 4.7 documentation; adopting 4.7.2 as the team patch is still a technical decision.

No gameplay scene or asset was modified or integrated. Editor import, terrain painting, collision, animation and lighting workflows are documented preparation steps requiring a separate runtime review. Existing Unreal art integration pages are historical and superseded for new artwork.

sections.title: Texture settings and verification
paragraphs: Keep PNG as a lossless runtime source and preserve editable Aseprite files separately. In Godot 4.7, filtering is a CanvasItem/project setting rather than the older per-image filter workflow. Set the project default under rendering/textures/canvas_textures/default_texture_filter to Nearest, or use a reviewed CanvasItem texture_filter override. Inspect inherited values on actual Sprite2D and TileMapLayer nodes.

For ordinary native-resolution sprites, use lossless compression and disable generated mipmaps as the initial recommendation. Mipmaps can help deliberate minification but are not a cure for noninteger scaling; approve them only with the camera policy. Keep alpha, avoid matte edges and examine transparent borders against both light and dark backgrounds. Texture import options are resource-specific; default filter, render size and stretch are project-wide unless overridden.

Atlas bleeding is addressed by correct regions, no unintended filtering and appropriate padding. TileSetAtlasSource supports use_texture_padding; retain and review it for its generated padding behavior rather than adding unexplained gaps to a zero-spacing atlas. Packed atlases need explicit rectangles and separation. Never apply a lossy compression setting that alters palette edges.

sections.title: Pixel-perfect presentation and Camera2D
paragraphs: Choose logical resolution only after gameplay and UI tests. Use the pixel-scale chapter’s 320×180, 384×216 and 480×270 candidates as comparisons, not approved settings. Godot viewport stretch can render at a fixed logical size; canvas_items stretch renders CanvasItem content at target resolution. The inspected project currently uses canvas_items/expand; this guide does not silently change it to a fixed viewport.

Use Camera2D for 2D view control. Integer zoom and presentation scaling keep consistent screen sample sizes. Pixel snapping options can affect transforms and vertices, but enabling every snap option without testing can create animation or camera jitter. Compare static camera, moving character, moving camera and camera smoothing separately. A smooth subpixel camera may make sprites shimmer; decide the presentation policy through runtime captures. Letterbox, expand or crop behavior must be documented for supported aspect ratios.

sections.title: TileSet and TileMapLayer setup
steps: Create a TileSet resource with tile_size (16,16), then add a TileSetAtlasSource referencing the native atlas PNG.
Set texture_region_size (16,16), margins (0,0) and separation (0,0) for this study. Create only the named occupied regions; leave intentional empty slots unused.
Define alternative tiles for compatible visual variants. Set reviewed TileData probability values if using weighted alternatives; keep terrain geometry and metadata compatible.
Create terrain sets and terrain modes suitable for the chosen kit. Map center and peering bits explicitly. Test all 47 binary patterns, empty boundaries and unsupported multi-material junctions.

Add TileSet physics layers and draw collision polygons only after gameplay review. Navigation layers and polygons require a separate navigation plan; occlusion layers require light testing. Custom data can carry reviewed art/integration metadata, not duplicate authoritative world state.
Configure animated atlas tiles for the water strip using animation columns and frame durations. Confirm the selected cells and full loop in-engine; four adjacent PNG cells do not animate themselves.

Use multiple TileMapLayer nodes for base ground, decoration and foreground as appropriate. Godot 4.7 TileMap is deprecated; use TileMapLayer for new work. Scene tiles through TileSetScenesCollectionSource are useful for actual reusable scene content, not required for every static prop.

sections.title: Origins, character nodes and shared timelines
paragraphs: With a centered 64×64 Sprite2D, the texture’s geometric center is (32,32). To place source contact (32,48) at the parent root, a visual offset of (0,-16) is the starting mapping. Verify it visually with the exported source: do not confuse texture center, node position and collision origin. AnimatedSprite2D supports centered sprites and offset too; record equivalent registration.

A flattened sprite can use AnimatedSprite2D and SpriteFrames. A layered character can use Sprite2D children and AnimationPlayer tracks, or a project-owned shared frame selector. All equipped layers share action, facing, frame and timeline. Exported Aseprite JSON needs an explicit importer or reviewed manual mapping; Godot does not preserve every Aseprite feature automatically. Retain original offsets if a packed sheet is later approved.

sections.title: Technical approval requires engine evidence
paragraphs: An integrator must verify filter inheritance, alpha, camera motion, aspect ratios, atlas coordinates, terrain painting, origin offsets, alternative tiles, water playback, collision, navigation where used, occlusion and paper-doll synchronization. Record exact Godot version, project commit and scene path for every pass. This edition does not claim those tests passed.

Artists supply clear source and visual contracts. Gameplay owns collision decisions, interaction logic, world state and networking. Do not introduce a plugin or a new mutable-state owner solely to explain an art export.

sections.title: Approval states
paragraphs: Use Draft → Ready for review → Revisions requested or Art approved → Technical validation pending → Production approved. Superseded records remain traceable. Art approval accepts appearance; technical approval accepts tested integration. Neither is inferred from a valid PNG or a passing documentation build.

A proposed reference can remain useful without production approval. A technical demonstration proves a specific construction or coordinate rule; it does not approve its art. An incorrect example must say what fails. Review records name the reviewer, date, asset ID, revision and evidence.

sections.title: Sixteen-point review
paragraphs: Check style compatibility, native density, dimensions, palette, silhouette, detail level, perspective, reusability, tile continuity, animation quality, frame registration, source structure, PNG export, Godot requirements, rights and gameplay readability. The printable checklist supplies explicit checkboxes and space for failure notes.

Review native-size and enlarged views. Zoom explains clusters, but 1× decides whether a silhouette reads. Compare exports to source hashes and registration. A sheet with correct dimensions can still contain the wrong action or missing diagonal direction.

sections.title: Review output
paragraphs: A review ends with Pass, Revisions requested or a documented test limitation, not an ambiguous aesthetic score. Block approval for unresolved rights, incomplete transition geometry or broken registration. Record minor polish separately so teams can prioritize structural fixes. Preserve screenshots and command results as evidence; never replace a failed check by weakening its rule.
